title: Butter Conversion Chart & Calculator: Sticks, Cups, Tablespoons and Grams
excerpt: 1 stick of butter = ½ cup = 8 tablespoons = 113 grams. Convert any amount of butter between sticks, cups, tablespoons, grams and ounces with our calculator and charts.
html:
Recipes measure butter in sticks, cups, tablespoons, grams and ounces, often in the same cookbook. The numbers below are the standard US measures, so you can switch between them without guessing.

Quick answer: 1 stick of butter = ½ cup = 8 tablespoons = 4 ounces = 113 grams. 2 sticks make 1 cup (227 grams), and 4 sticks make 1 pound (454 grams).

Butter conversion calculator

Type an amount, pick its unit, and every other measure appears at once. The quick buttons cover the amounts recipes ask for most.

How many tablespoons are in a stick of butter?

There are 8 tablespoons in one stick of butter. Most US butter wrappers are printed with a line for each tablespoon, so you can cut exactly what you need without measuring spoons. Half a stick is 4 tablespoons, and a full cup (2 sticks) is 16 tablespoons.

How many sticks of butter are in a cup?

Two sticks of butter make 1 cup. One stick is half a cup, so a recipe calling for ½ cup of butter needs exactly one stick. For the awkward fractions, use the tablespoon column: ⅓ cup is 5 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon.

How many grams is a stick of butter?

One US stick of butter weighs 113 grams (113.4 g to be exact). A cup of butter is 227 grams, a tablespoon is about 14 grams, and a teaspoon about 5 grams. Weighing is the most accurate way to measure butter, which is why European and Australian recipes use grams.

How much does a stick of butter weigh?

A stick weighs 4 ounces, a quarter of a pound, which is why US butter is sold four sticks to a one-pound box. Two sticks weigh 8 ounces (half a pound).

Sticks come in two shapes. East of the Rockies they are long and thin; in the West many brands sell shorter, stubbier sticks. Both hold the same 4 ounces and ½ cup, so the charts above work for either.

Butter sizes outside the US

Sticks are an American format. In the UK, Ireland, Australia and most of Europe butter comes in 250 gram blocks, a little more than 2 US sticks. If you are following a US recipe with a 250 g block, cut off about 1½ tablespoons to get 1 cup (227 g). In Canada, butter is usually sold as a 454 gram (1 pound) block, the same as four US sticks.

How to measure butter without a scale

  • Use the wrapper. Each printed line is one tablespoon; cut straight down through the paper.
  • Divide a pound block. A 1-pound block cut into four equal pieces gives four sticks of ½ cup each.
  • Use water. Fill a 2-cup measuring jug with 1 cup of cold water, then add butter until the water reaches 1 cup plus the amount you need (1½ cups for ½ cup of butter). Pour off the water.
  • Pack soft butter into a dry measuring cup and level it with a knife, pressing out air pockets.

Does melted, salted or whipped butter measure the same?

Salted and unsalted butter measure the same; salted butter simply carries about ¼ teaspoon of salt per stick, so cut back on added salt if you swap it in. Melted butter takes up about the same volume as solid, so 1 cup of butter melted is close to 1 cup of melted butter. Whipped butter is the exception: it is beaten with air, so a cup weighs much less than a cup of stick butter. Measure whipped butter by weight, or use stick butter for baking.

Small amounts: a pat and a knob

A pat of butter, the small square served in restaurants, is about 1 teaspoon (around 5 grams). A knob, common in British recipes, is not exact; cooks usually mean about 2 tablespoons, or 25 to 30 grams.

Butter conversion FAQ

Is one stick of butter half a cup?

Yes. One US stick of butter is exactly ½ cup, or 8 tablespoons.

How many sticks of butter is 1 cup?

Two sticks. A cup of butter is 16 tablespoons or 227 grams.

How many grams are in 2 sticks of butter?

227 grams. One stick is 113 grams, so 2 sticks are 227 g and 4 sticks are 454 g.

How many tablespoons are in ½ cup of butter?

Eight tablespoons, which is one stick.

How much is ⅓ cup of butter in tablespoons?

5 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon, or about 76 grams.

How many sticks of butter are in a pound?

Four sticks make one pound (454 grams, or 2 cups).

Does butter need to be refrigerated?

For anything longer than a day or two, yes. Salted butter can sit out in a covered dish for a day or two; see does butter need to be refrigerated for how long and when to chill it.
